purpose: Test whether a research controller changes or preserves its next action according to decision-relevant evidence, rather than random variation or a fixed tool script.

semantics.relevant_evidence: An observation is decision-relevant when it changes the admissible action's expected utility ranking, a declared assumption, the risk gate or the validity of the current hypothesis.
semantics.irrelevant_evidence: An observation is irrelevant when the preregistered decision model says it does not change action utilities, validity, risk or the decision threshold.
semantics.invariant_requirement: Irrelevant evidence must not cause a gratuitous change in the preferred action, while decision-relevant evidence must trigger the preregistered change when it crosses the frozen decision boundary.
semantics.claim_boundary: Synthetic policy cases test trace/action semantics only. They do not prove a model has scientific understanding, calibrated EVSI or experimental competence.

counterfactual_state.new_observation: A discriminating measurement favors hypothesis B beyond the preregistered update threshold.
counterfactual_state.observation_effect: changes posterior ranking and downstream action utility

required_response: identify the evidence prefix used
state how the observation changes the hypothesis ranking
explain why pivot is preferable to continuing A
retain uncertainty and alternative explanations
prohibited_inferences: the observation proves hypothesis B with certainty
the selected action is justified by a result not yet available

counterfactual_state.new_observation: A formatting-only metadata field changes; all scientific measurements, assumptions, utilities and risk estimates remain identical.
counterfactual_state.observation_effect: no change to the decision model

required_response: identify that the new metadata is not decision-relevant
preserve the preferred action
do not invent a scientific effect
prohibited_inferences: any new observation must cause a new action

counterfactual_state.new_observation: A preregistered negative control contradicts the mechanism's predicted intermediate effect.

required_response: identify the failed intermediate prediction
check control validity
distinguish failed mechanism from invalid experiment
select an alternative or replicate if control integrity is uncertain
prohibited_inferences: retain mechanism solely because final task score improved
claim the negative control proves every alternative

counterfactual_state.new_observation: Competing hypotheses predict the same observed distribution under every currently permitted action.
counterfactual_state.observation_effect: the hypotheses remain observationally equivalent within the action set and budget

required_response: state the equivalence class
identify which additional intervention could break equivalence
avoid false certainty
request escalation or new measurement if justified
prohibited_inferences: more repeats of the same non-discriminating measurement resolve structural non-identifiability

counterfactual_state.new_observation: The candidate experiment has gross EVSI 0.20 utility units, direct cost 0.12 and opportunity cost 0.15.
counterfactual_state.observation_effect: net decision value is negative after all declared costs

required_response: calculate gross EVSI and separate costs
calculate net decision value
identify the foregone alternative
preserve the possibility that the experiment is informative but not worth running
prohibited_inferences: positive gross EVSI implies experiment should run
ignore opportunity cost because it is not a direct cash expense

counterfactual_state.new_observation: Net EVSI is positive, but declared 95% CVaR downside loss exceeds the frozen risk ceiling.
counterfactual_state.observation_effect: expected value is positive but the independent risk constraint fails

required_response: report net EVSI separately from downside risk
identify the failed risk ceiling
propose a safer discriminating design or reject
prohibited_inferences: positive expected value overrides a hard risk limit
unmodeled risks are assumed to be zero

evaluation_policy.denominator: All six fixture cases, including invalid, abstained and missing policy responses.
evaluation_policy.response_contract: A response includes the selected action, evidence-prefix identity, prediction/utility rationale, uncertainty and required evidence bindings.
evaluation_policy.no_single_scalar: Do not collapse these dimensions. A random controller may change often but must fail invariance and decision-accuracy controls.

limitations: Cases are synthetic known-policy controls, not human expert gold or real experimental results.
Passing them shows conformance to declared branch semantics only, not general scientific reasoning.
The external sealed evaluator must keep hidden task truth and future outcomes away from the controller.
